title: Volume and Surface Area of Solids

blocks.text: How many litres does a cylindrical water tank hold? How much paint covers a dome? Volume answers the first question and surface area the second — and mixing them up is the fastest way to lose marks in this section of the paper.

blocks.markdown:
### Prisms are the easy case

A **prism** is a solid with the same cross-section all the way through. For any prism,

$$\text{volume} = \text{area of cross-section} \times \text{length}$$

A cylinder is a prism whose cross-section is a circle, so its volume is $\pi r^2 h$. A cuboid is a prism whose cross-section is a rectangle.

rows: Base + area of the sloping faces
blocks.caption: l is the slant height for a cone, and h is always the perpendicular height

blocks.title: The one-third rule
blocks.text: A cone or pyramid holds exactly **one third** of the prism with the same base and height. That is where the $\frac{1}{3}$ comes from, and it is a useful check: a cone's volume must be much smaller than the cylinder that encloses it.

blocks.title: Volume of a cone from the slant height
blocks.prompt: A cone has base radius 5 cm and slant height 13 cm. Find its volume, taking π = 22/7.

steps.text: The volume formula needs the perpendicular height h, not the slant height l. The radius, height and slant height form a right-angled triangle.
Now substitute into the cone volume formula.
Simplify: 25 × 12 = 300, and one third of 300 is 100.

blocks.markdown:
### Curved versus total surface area

Read the question carefully:

- **Curved surface area** is only the wrapped-round part.
- **Total surface area** adds the flat ends.

A closed cylinder has two circular ends, so its total surface area is $2\pi r h + 2\pi r^2$. An open cylindrical tank, such as a bucket, has only one end, so it is $2\pi r h + \pi r^2$. The word "open" or "closed" in the question decides the answer.

blocks.caption: Capacity conversions needed for tank and container questions

items: Density = mass ÷ volume, so mass = density × volume.
Capacity questions usually want litres, so convert from m³ or cm³ at the end.
Keep π as 22/7 in fraction form until the last step to avoid rounding errors.
Check that a volume answer has cubic units and a surface area answer has square units.

blocks.title: Slant height or perpendicular height?
blocks.text: For a cone, **volume** uses the perpendicular height $h$ while **curved surface area** uses the slant height $l$. They are linked by $l^2 = r^2 + h^2$. Examiners routinely give one and require the other, so expect to use Pythagoras first.

points: For a prism, volume is cross-sectional area times length.
A cone or pyramid has one third the volume of the prism with the same base and height.
The volume of a sphere is $\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3$ and its surface area is $4\pi r^2$.
Curved surface area excludes the flat ends; total surface area includes them.
A cone's volume needs the perpendicular height, but its curved surface area needs the slant height.
